3 - Verify a logged-in customer with an EMPTY cart hitting /checkout/ directly is redirected to Cart's own empty-cart state
NEW, 2026-08-13. Confirmed live: a real Magento redirect, not a broken empty Shipping step — distinct from test 1 (guest + populated cart, blocked with a login message) in that this is a logged-in customer with nothing in cart at all, redirected to /checkout/cart/'s empty state instead. Relies on test 2's login persisting in this suite's shared browser context, same as every other test below it in this file — does NOT attempt its own fresh login, since navigating to /customer/account/login/ while already authenticated redirects to the account dashboard instead of showing the login form, which silently broke this test's first 3 steps when originally authored with its own login attempt (caught via a real full-suite run, not assumed). Still self-contained in the sense that matters: explicitly empties the cart first rather than assuming a clean starting state. IMPORTANT: restores a real item to cart at the end of its own steps (after the empty-state assertion) — every test below this one in the file relies on an item already being in cart (a continuity assumption already baked into the original file, going back to test 2 being the one that first adds the item), and this test would otherwise silently strand the cart empty for everything downstream. Caught via a real full-suite run where this omission cascaded into failures on tests 4 through 15 that have nothing to do with this test's own subject — a costly lesson in checking what a new test leaves behind, not just what it itself asserts. Removes up to 20 cart lines one at a time (not just one) — this account's cart is real, persistent server-side state shared across every run of this suite (not reset between runs), and it grows by design: tests 16 and 17 each add real items/coupons without cleaning up after themselves (kept that way deliberately rather than adding self-cleanup complexity to tests whose own subject is unrelated to cart hygiene), so leftover items accumulate across repeated runs — a first attempt at 6 removals still wasn't enough after several runs in one session, caught live via an actual full-suite failure, not assumed sufficient in advance. 20 is a generous safety margin for normal usage; if this suite is ever run dozens of times in a single day again, reconsider a bulk-clear mechanism instead of continuing to raise this number.

Used `:has-text()` (substring match) instead.

# Action Expected / Result Status
#01 Typing "ABCDE" into Kode Pos and "not-a-phone-number!!" into Nomor Telepon in the Add New Address popup is accepted with no client-side format validation of any kind — both fields are plain `type="text"` with only a `required` (presence) constraint, no numeric/phone pattern.
⚠ ErrorTyping "ABCDE" into Kode Pos and "not-a-phone-number!!" into Nomor Telepon in the Add New Address popup is accepted with no client-side format validation of any kind — both fields are plain `type="text"` with only a `required` (presence) constraint, no numeric/phone pattern.
🖼️ Live Page Screenshot — the actual front-end element click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
[A] WEBSITE BUG — the Kode Pos and Nomor Telepon <input> elements in the Add New Address popup are rendered as plain type="text" with only required="", missing any pattern/inputmode/type="tel" constraint that would reject non-numeric input client-side.
❌ Problematic Code
Not visible from the front end — lives in the Kemana_ShipperLogistic
checkout address-form template/knockout bindings that render these two
`<input>` elements; likely a copy-paste from a generic text-field
pattern rather than a numeric-specific one.
✅ Fixed Code
Add a numeric pattern/inputmode to both fields, e.g.
`<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" pattern="[0-9]+" ...>` for Kode
Pos, and an Indonesian phone-number pattern (e.g.
`pattern="^(\+62|0)[0-9]{8,13}{{SCENARIOS}}quot;`) for Nomor Telepon, with matching
server-side validation (client-side alone is not sufficient).
📋 What To Do
1. Add client-side pattern/inputmode constraints to both fields in the address-form template. 2. Confirm server-side validation independently rejects non-numeric postcode/phone values on the actual save endpoint — client-side validation alone is bypassable and should not be the only safeguard. 3. Re-test by attempting to save an address with a non-numeric Kode Pos and Nomor Telepon and confirming both are rejected with a clear message, not silently accepted.
